original_question: 3NF और BCNF के बीच प्राथमिक अंतर क्या है?

retrieved_chunks_details.subject: dbms
retrieved_chunks_details.text: Relational Database Normalization: 1NF to BCNF Normalization is the systematic design process of organizing data to eliminate insertion, update, and deletion anomalies while minimizing data redundancy. - First Normal Form (1NF): A relation is in 1NF if every attribute domain contains only atomic (indivisible) values and each row is unique. - Second Normal Form (2NF): A relation is in 2NF if it is in 1NF and no non-prime attribute is partially dependent on any candidate key. - Third Normal Form (3NF): A relation is in 3NF if it is in 2NF and no non-prime attribute is transitively dependent on candidate keys (for every functional dependency X -> A, either X is a superkey or A is a prime attribute). - Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF): A stricter version of 3NF where for every non-trivial functional dependency X -> A, X must be a superkey.

retrieved_chunks_details.subject: computer_networks
retrieved_chunks_details.text: Computer Networks: Transport Layer Protocols and TCP 3-Way Handshake The Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) is a connection-oriented, reliable, byte-stream transport layer protocol defined in RFC 793. Unlike UDP, which is connectionless and best-effort, TCP provides guaranteed in-order delivery, flow control, and congestion control. Before data transfer begins, TCP establishes a virtual connection between client and server using a Three-Way Handshake: 1. SYN: The active client generates a randomly chosen Initial Sequence Number (ISN_client = x) and sends a TCP segment with the SYN control flag set to 1. 2. SYN-ACK: The passive server receives the SYN segment, allocates connection buffers and state variables, generates its own Initial Sequence Number (ISN_server = y), and transmits a segment with SYN=1 and ACK=1, where the acknowledgment number is set to x + 1. 3. ACK: The client receives the SYN-ACK, transitions to the ESTABLISHED state, and transmits an ACK segment with ACK=1 and acknowledgment number set to y + 1. Data payloads can accompany this third packet.

retrieved_chunks_details.subject: computer_networks
retrieved_chunks_details.text: TCP Flow Control vs Congestion Control It is vital to distinguish between flow control and congestion control in computer networks: - Flow Control is a speed-matching service that prevents a fast sender from overwhelming a slow receiver's buffer space. TCP implements flow control using a receive window (`rwnd`) field in the TCP header. The receiver explicitly informs the sender of how many spare bytes of buffer space are currently available (`rwnd = RcvBuffer - [LastByteRcvd - LastByteRead]`). The sender ensures that the unacknowledged data never exceeds `rwnd`. - Congestion Control prevents senders from injecting too much traffic into the network subnet, avoiding packet loss and queue collapse in intermediate routers. TCP maintains a congestion window (`cwnd`). The effective transmission window is $\min(\text{cwnd}, \text{rwnd})$. TCP congestion control algorithms (such as TCP Reno and Tahoe) employ four phases: Slow Start (exponential window growth), Congestion Avoidance (additive increase / multiplicative decrease, AIMD), Fast Retransmit, and Fast Recovery.

retrieved_chunks_details.text: OSI Reference Model vs TCP/IP Protocol Stack The Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) reference model, developed by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO), is a conceptual framework with seven distinct architectural layers: 1. Physical Layer: Transmission and reception of raw unstructured bit streams over physical media. 2. Data Link Layer: Node-to-node frame transfer, media access control (MAC), and error detection (CRC). 3. Network Layer: Multi-hop routing, packet forwarding, and logical addressing (IPv4, IPv6). 4. Transport Layer: End-to-end process-to-process communication, multiplexing (TCP, UDP). 5. Session Layer: Dialog control, token management, and synchronization checkpoints. 6. Presentation Layer: Syntax translation, character encoding, data compression, and encryption/SSL. 7. Application Layer: High-level network application services (HTTP, DNS, SMTP, FTP). In contrast, the practical TCP/IP Internet model consolidates the top three layers into a single Application Layer, resulting in a streamlined four-layer stack: Network Interface (Link), Internet (IP), Transport (TCP/UDP), and Application.

retrieved_chunks_details.subject: automata
retrieved_chunks_details.text: Context-Free Grammars and Pushdown Automata Context-Free Grammars (CFGs) generate the class of context-free languages, which strictly subsume regular languages. A CFG is a 4-tuple (V, Sigma, R, S), where V is a finite set of non-terminal variables, Sigma is the terminal alphabet, R is a finite set of production rules of the form A -> alpha with A in V and alpha in (V union Sigma)*, and S is the start symbol. A Pushdown Automaton (PDA) is the mechanical equivalent of a CFG. It extends a finite state machine with an unbounded Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) stack storage. Deterministic Pushdown Automata (DPDAs) recognize deterministic context-free languages, which form a strict subset of context-free languages recognized by non-deterministic PDAs (e.g., the language of palindromes {w w^R}).
